ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 2, a charged small ball A of mass m is suspended from point O on the ceiling by an insulating silk thin string of length l. On an insulating support at a point l directly below O, a small ball B carrying the same kind of charge as A is fixed. Both charged small balls may be regarded as point charges. It is known that when small ball A is at rest, the angle between the string OA and the vertical direction is 60°. Let the tension in the string be T, and the Coulomb force on the small ball be F. Which of the following relational expressions is correct? (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 2, a charged small ball A of mass m is suspended from point O on the ceiling by an insulating silk thin string of length l. On an insulating support at a point l directly below O, a small ball B carrying the same kind of charge as A is fixed. Both charged small balls may be regarded as point charges. It is known that when small ball A is at rest, the angle between the string OA and the vertical direction is 60°. Find the relationship between the Coulomb force F on small ball A and mg.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, below the ceiling there is a suspension point O, and charged small ball A is suspended at the lower right of point O by a thin string OA labeled l; directly below point O there is a vertical dashed line, beside the dashed line is labeled l, indicating that fixed small ball B is located at a distance l directly below point O; the figure marks the angle between OA and the vertical direction OB as 60°. Then reason: from the figure and the meaning of the problem, it can be known that OA=l, OB=l, and ∠AOB=60°, so △AOB is an equilateral triangle, and AB=l. Small balls A and B carry the same kind of charge, so A is subjected to the Coulomb repulsive force F from B along the direction BA, away from B; the tension T in the thin string is along direction AO and points to O; the gravity mg is vertically downward. Since △AOB is equilateral, at A the direction AO of the tension and the direction BA of the Coulomb force are symmetric about the vertical direction, and the angles between both of them and the vertically upward direction are 60°. Small ball A is at rest, and the resultant force in the horizontal direction is zero, giving Tsin60°=Fsin60°, so T=F. The resultant force in the vertical direction is zero, giving Tcos60°+Fcos60°=mg. Substituting T=F and cos60°=1/2 gives F=mg.
